title: Chasing Sunrise on the Ridge (Solo Overnight, Fog Everywhere)
creator: Tomas Lindqvist
description:
Hiked up to the ridge for sunrise and got completely fogged in. Then it cleared. Sort of.

Shot on a Sony a7 IV with the 24-105 and a 70-200.

Some of the links below are affiliate links. If you buy through them I may earn a small commission, which helps keep the channel going.

My pack: https://www.rei.com/affiliate/tl-pack
Camera clip: https://bhpho.to/3Tq8LkP
Tripod: https://bhpho.to/4aWm0Zd
Headlamp: https://amzn.to/3RkLq2v

Music: Epidemic Sound
Prints: tomaslindqvist.photo

sentences.t: It is three forty in the morning and I have been walking uphill for an hour and a half.
The plan was simple, get to the ridge before sunrise, shoot the valley with the fog sitting in it.
The problem is I am currently inside the fog.
Like, I can see maybe ten meters, and that's with the headlamp on full.
So we'll see, we'll see if this works out.
Okay, I made it to the top, and it is just white, everywhere, in every direction.
This is kind of the gamble with fog, right?
If you're above it, you get this incredible sea of clouds, and if you're in it, you get nothing.
The forecast said the cloud base would be around eight hundred meters and I'm at about nine fifty.
So in theory I should be above it, which, clearly, I'm not.
I'm going to set up anyway and just wait, because sometimes it drops right at sunrise when the air warms up.
Tripod out, I'm going to put the long lens on because if it clears I want to compress those layers.
It's cold, it's like two degrees, and my fingers are not loving the metal on this thing.
Okay, look, look over there.
Can you see that, the top of that peak is just poking through.
It's starting to sink, this is it, this is what I came for.
I'm going to shut up and shoot for a minute.
Oh, that's so good, the light is just hitting the edge of the cloud now.
This is around sixteen hundred millimeters equivalent if you crop in, no, I'm kidding, it's two hundred.
But the compression makes the ridges look like they're stacked right on top of each other.
I'm bracketing these, three exposures, because the sky is so much brighter than the valley.
And it's going, it's going, it's closing back in.
That was maybe six minutes total, which honestly in fog is a gift.
Let me look at what I got.
Okay, this one, I think this is the one, with the single tree on the left edge.
The fog is lit from behind so it kind of glows, and the tree is just a silhouette.
I'll do a proper edit when I get home, but I'm really happy with that.
Now the less glamorous part, which is walking back down for two hours on wet rock.
I always tell people, sunrise hikes are only half about the sunrise.
The other half is not falling over on the way down when you're tired and your knees are done.
Take poles, honestly, I resisted for years and now I won't go without them.
Okay, I'm back at the car, it's nine in the morning and I want a very large breakfast.
Before I go, people always ask about the gear, so here's the quick rundown.
The pack is a thirty eight liter from REI, the camera clip on my shoulder strap is the Peak Design Capture, and the tripod is a little carbon travel one.
The headlamp is a Petzl, and I'd genuinely say that's the most important thing I carried today.
All of it's linked below, and a few of those are affiliate links, so I get a small cut if you buy through them, at no extra cost to you.
None of these companies sent me anything, I bought it all, and it's just what I've ended up using after a lot of trial and error.
If you've got older gear that works, keep using it, seriously.
The edit of that tree shot is going up on my Instagram later this week.
And if there's a spot near you that you think I should try for fog, drop it in the comments.
Thanks for coming up the mountain with me, I'll see you on the next one.
